node.title: Re^5: The most precise second (timer)
node.author: soonix
node.doctext:
the different length of your results, and especially the trailing "M" in the last line made me suspect gettimeofday doesn't return integers. A look into [mod://Time::HiRes] confirms
gettimeofday ()
In array context returns a two-element array with the seconds and microseconds since the epoch. In scalar context returns floating seconds like Time::HiRes::time()
[doc://print] evaluates its arguments in array context. So you could either change $, ($OUTPUT_FIELD_SEPARATOR) to somethng visible, or force scalar context by printing scalar gettimeofday or gettimeofday+0.
